title: Why does your muscle pull harder?
hook: The load and the muscle pull at very different distances from your elbow.

knows: the quantities named in the question
doesNotKnow: Balance the turning effects: 20 N × 30 cm = muscle force × 4 cm. The muscle needs 150 N because its moment arm is much shorter.

misconception: The alternative answers in the prediction appear plausible without the stated physical model.
objective: Balance the turning effects: 20 N × 30 cm = muscle force × 4 cm. The muscle needs 150 N because its moment arm is much shorter.

claims.text: Balance the turning effects: 20 N × 30 cm = muscle force × 4 cm. The muscle needs 150 N because its moment arm is much shorter. Static, perpendicular forces; arm weight and other muscles are ignored.
claims.source: Torque equilibrium: F_m × 4 cm = 20 N × r. For r=10 cm F_m=50 N; for r=30 cm F_m=150 N.

recall.question: A 10 N load is 20 cm from the pivot. A muscle pulls at 5 cm, perpendicular to the lever. What force balances it?
